learningObjectives.title: Types of force and free-body diagrams

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explain: Force is measured in newtons (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-contact force?
questions.explain: Gravitational force acts at a distance without objects touching, so it is a non-contact force.

questions.q: What does a free-body diagram show?
options: All the forces acting on a single object
The motion of two colliding objects
The energy stored in an object
The path an object travels over time
questions.explain: A free-body diagram isolates one object and shows every force acting on it as an arrow.

questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: Force is a vector because it has both magnitude and direction.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure the size of a force?
questions.explain: A newtonmeter (spring balance) measures force in newtons using an extending spring.

questions.q: What is meant by the resultant force on an object?
options: The single force that has the same effect as all the forces acting together
The largest force acting on the object
The force of gravity on the object
The force needed to keep the object still
questions.explain: The resultant is the overall force found by combining all individual forces acting on an object.

questions.q: A box has a force of 8 N acting to the right and 3 N acting to the left. What is the resultant force?
questions.explain: For forces in opposite directions the resultant is the difference: 8 N - 3 N = 5 N to the right.

questions.q: Which equation represents Newton's second law of motion?
questions.explain: Newton's second law states resultant force equals mass multiplied by acceleration, F = ma.

questions.q: A car travels at a constant velocity in a straight line. What can you conclude about the forces on it?
options: The driving force is greater than friction
There are no forces acting on the car
questions.explain: By Newton's first law, constant velocity means the forces are balanced and the resultant force is zero.

questions.q: Which statement best expresses Newton's third law of motion?
options: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
An object stays still unless pushed
questions.explain: Newton's third law: when object A exerts a force on B, B exerts an equal and opposite force on A.

questions.q: According to Newton's first law, if the resultant force on an object is zero, the object will:
options: Remain at rest or continue at constant velocity
questions.explain: Newton's first law states an object keeps its state of rest or uniform motion unless a resultant force acts.

questions.q: A resultant force of 12 N acts on a 3 kg mass. What is its acceleration?
questions.explain: Using a = F/m = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 m/s².

questions.q: A trolley of mass 5 kg experiences a resultant force of 20 N. What is its acceleration?
questions.explain: Rearranging F = ma gives a = F/m = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 m/s².

questions.q: If the resultant force on an object is doubled while its mass stays the same, its acceleration will:
questions.explain: Since a = F/m, acceleration is directly proportional to force, so doubling the force doubles the acceleration.

questions.q: Which equation is used to calculate the weight of an object?
questions.explain: Weight equals mass multiplied by gravitational field strength, W = mg.

questions.q: In which unit is mass measured?
questions.explain: Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and is measured in kilograms (kg).

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass is the amount of matter in an object; weight is the force of gravity on it
Mass is a force; weight is the amount of matter
Mass and weight are the same thing
Mass is measured in newtons; weight in kilograms
questions.explain: Mass (kg) measures the matter present, while weight (N) is the gravitational force acting on that mass.

questions.q: Calculate the weight of a 6 kg object on Earth, where g = 9.8 N/kg.
questions.explain: Using W = mg = 6 × 9.8 = 58.8 N.

questions.q: A skydiver reaches terminal velocity. What is true about the forces acting on them?
options: Weight is greater than air resistance
Air resistance equals weight, so the resultant force is zero
questions.explain: At terminal velocity the upward air resistance balances the downward weight, giving zero resultant force and constant velocity.

questions.q: What is the approximate value of the gravitational field strength (g) at the Earth's surface?
questions.explain: The gravitational field strength at the Earth's surface is about 9.8 N/kg.
